record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss scaling in jet classification and reports distinct exponents, broken power laws for some feature settings, and fit-dependent results. These findings refine the scope of scaling-law claims.
record.gate_note: The study trains six classifiers on top-versus-QCD jets and measures binary cross-entropy test loss as training-set size varies. It does not test whether small runs predict actual much larger runs, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream-task performance. Claims about those topics cited from other work are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests power-law loss scaling in a new setting: supervised classification of simulated particle jets. Its own results bear on V5 and V7, including broken scaling curves and sensitivity to fitting choices.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find power-law test-loss scaling over 3–4 decades in simulated jet classification, with classifier-dependent slopes and changing rankings. They identify broken laws and fitting uncertainty, and present eventual LOT-DNN superiority as an unvalidated extrapolation requiring larger datasets.
record.recipe_differences: This is an extension to simulated jet classification rather than a reproduction of language-model scaling experiments. It varies training-set size and measures binary cross-entropy for six physically motivated classifiers; it does not sweep language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Classifier and input representation change the fitted slope; LR feature count gives broken power laws; including a nonzero loss floor changes the DNN fitted slopes; EMD R changes the loss coefficient but not the slope; LOT reference-jet size has no reported effect.
record.problems: The evidence is from one simulated jet-classification task and six classifiers. The authors report noisy behavior at small training-set sizes, limit EMD to T ≤ 3.5 × 104 for computational reasons, and note that fit uncertainties omit other sources of error. Some additional curve comparisons are shown only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant test-loss results were intentionally omitted. Data covariance spectra and correlation-dimension measurements (Fig. 4) concern possible explanations for scaling and do not directly measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss or parameter/token/compute scaling.
Extrapolations are not validated against actual runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute optimisation of model size and training-data allocation.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count; tripling width and depth changes parameter count.
Tests simulated jet classification only; image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested.
No downstream evaluation linked to pretraining loss or pretrained-model scale.
No compute-optimal split, parameter-counting conventions, training-schedule sweep, or explanation of disagreements among published language-model laws.

missing.what: A genuine kNN EFP scaling break around T = 50, explicitly distinguished from noise; the existing exponent row covers only T ≥ 500.
Nonzero-floor fits are much poorer for kNN EMD, kNN EFP and LR EFP, with order-one uncertainty in C; this qualifies comparisons of floor-based exponents.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source of the listed versions. T3 best captures its primary contribution, with additional qualifying evidence relevant to T5. For R10–R15, the single state describes partial agreement with V5; the same bends are observed evidence for V7. Reported fit errors exclude other uncertainty sources.

versions.untested_parts: The study concerns jet-classification loss versus training-set size, not held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
It extrapolates fitted curves but does not compare predictions with actual runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is tested.
The study does not systematically vary depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests simulated top-versus-QCD jet classification as training-set size varies; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The measured loss is the classification task's own test loss, not downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.

Tests dependence on classifier/input-feature choices and on fitting with or without a loss floor. It does not test parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, language-model data choices, or the compute-optimal split.
